items.title: Compactness of the finite complex Grassmannian
items.design_state: Step 1 argument and contract are complete; current native readiness record is ready.
items.statement: Let $N\ge2$. For $1\le k<N$, let $\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$ be the set of matrices $P\in M_N(\mathbb C)$ satisfying $P^*=P$, $P^2=P$, and $\operatorname{tr}P=k$, with the topology inherited from $M_N(\mathbb C)\cong\mathbb R^{2N^2}$. The map $P\mapsto\operatorname{ran}P$ identifies this space with the usual Grassmannian of complex $k$-planes in $\mathbb C^N$. The finite union $\mathscr G_N=\bigcup_{1\le k<N}\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$ is compact.

references.title: I. M. Singer, Some Remarks on the Gribov Ambiguity, Communications in Mathematical Physics 60 (1978), 7–12
references.locator: §2, p. 9, irreducible holonomy and finite-dimensional Grassmannian context; compactness proof supplied locally.

references.locator: §5.13.2–§5.13.3, PDF pp. 114–116, Sobolev connection/gauge setup and irreducibility convention; Grassmannian compactness is proved locally.

items.title: Dimension of the finite holonomy incidence manifold
items.design_state: Step 1 argument and contract are complete; current native readiness record is ready.
items.statement:
Let $N\ge2$, $r\ge1$, and $1\le k<N$. For each orthogonal projection $P$ onto a complex $k$-plane in $\mathbb C^N$, write $V_P=\operatorname{ran}P$. Define
$$
I_{k,r}=\{(g_1,\ldots,g_r,P)\in SU(N)^r\times\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N):g_iV_P=V_P\text{ for every }i\},
$$
where $SU(N)$ has its usual matrix Lie-group structure and $\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$ has the orthogonal-projection topology. Then $I_{k,r}$ is a closed embedded smooth submanifold,
$$
\dim I_{k,r}=2k(N-k)+r\bigl(k^2+(N-k)^2-1\bigr).
$$
Its codimension in $SU(N)^r\times\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$ is $2r\,k(N-k)$, and
$$
\dim SU(N)^r-\dim I_{k,r}=2(r-1)k(N-k).
$$

references.title: I. M. Singer, Some Remarks on the Gribov Ambiguity, Communications in Mathematical Physics 60 (1978), 7–12
references.locator: §2, pp. 8–10, irreducible holonomy and the reducible locus; the finite-dimensional incidence calculation is proved locally.

references.locator: §1, pp. 2–3, stabilizers of irreducible connections; the finite-dimensional incidence calculation is proved locally.

items.title: Finite holonomy witnesses for irreducibility
items.design_state: Step 1 argument and contract are complete; current direct and transitive inputs have ready records. This does not claim independent proof approval.
items.statement: Assume ZF together with the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be $S^3$ or $S^4$ with its compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth structure and a smooth Riemannian metric. Let $N\ge2$, let $P\to M$ be a smooth principal right $SU(N)$-bundle, choose a smooth reference connection $A_0$, a basepoint $m\in M$, and a frame of the fiber $P_m$. Put $\mathcal A_\infty=A_0+\Omega^1(M;\operatorname{ad}P)$ with its $C^\infty$ section topology. For a smooth connection $A$, let $\operatorname{Hol}_A\subseteq SU(N)$ be the group generated by parallel transports along based piecewise-smooth loops at $m$, expressed in the chosen frame. Call $A$ irreducible when the standard action of $\operatorname{Hol}_A$ on $\mathbb C^N$ has no nonzero proper invariant complex subspace, and write $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ for this locus. For each integer $q>\dim(M)/2+1$, let $\mathcal G_{q+1}$ be the $H^{q+1}$ gauge group of sections of $\operatorname{Ad}P$, acting on $H^q$ connections by the local formula $A^u=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$, and let $Z_N=\{\zeta I_N:\zeta^N=1\}$. Measure $C^1$ closeness by coefficient and first-derivative suprema in a fixed finite bundle atlas. For every $A\in\mathcal A_\infty^*$, a finite tuple of based piecewise-smooth loops has holonomies with no common nonzero proper invariant subspace; the same tuple continues to witness irreducibility on a $C^1$ neighborhood of $A$, so $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is open in the $C^\infty$ topology. The stabilizer of $A$ in $\mathcal G_{q+1}$ is exactly $Z_N$. Irreducibility here does not assert $\operatorname{Hol}_A=SU(N)$.

references.title: I. M. Singer, Some Remarks on the Gribov Ambiguity, Communications in Mathematical Physics 60 (1978), 7–12
references.locator: §2, pp. 8–9, holonomy irreducibility, central stabilizer and openness; the finite-witness argument is supplied locally.

references.locator: §1, pp. 2–3, gauge action, irreducible connections and stabilizers; the finite-witness argument is supplied locally.

items.title: Relative finite-parameter avoidance of reducible connections
items.design_state: Step 1 argument and contract are complete; current direct and transitive inputs have ready records. This does not claim independent proof approval.
items.statement: Assume ZF together with the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be $S^3$ or $S^4$ with its compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth structure, let $N\ge2$, and let $P\to M$ be a smooth principal right $SU(N)$-bundle with a smooth reference connection $A_0$. Fix a basepoint $m\in M$ and a frame of $P_m$. Equip $\mathcal A_\infty=A_0+\Omega^1(M;\operatorname{ad}P)$ with the Fréchet topology generated by suprema of all derivatives of section coefficients in a fixed finite bundle atlas. Let $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ consist of connections whose based holonomy action on $\mathbb C^N$ has no nonzero proper invariant complex subspace. Let $K$ be the geometric realization of a finite simplicial complex, let $L$ be the realization of a subcomplex, and let $f:K\to\mathcal A_\infty$ be continuous with $f(L)\subseteq\mathcal A_\infty^*$. Then there is a continuous homotopy $H:K\times[0,1]\to\mathcal A_\infty$, fixed on $L$ and on an open neighborhood of $L$, such that $H(\cdot,1)$ maps all of $K$ into $\mathcal A_\infty^*$. For every finite list of these $C^\infty$ section seminorms $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ and positive tolerances $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_m$, the homotopy can be chosen with $\sup_{(s,t)\in K\times[0,1]}p_j(H(s,t)-f(s))<\epsilon_j$ for every $j$.

references.title: I. M. Singer, Some Remarks on the Gribov Ambiguity, Communications in Mathematical Physics 60 (1978), 7–12
references.locator: Theorem 2, p. 9, weak homotopy type; the infinite-codimension outline is not used as a complete proof.

items.title: Weak contractibility of the irreducible connection locus
items.design_state: Step 1 argument and contract are complete; current direct and transitive inputs have ready records. This does not claim independent proof approval.
items.statement: Assume ZF together with the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be $S^3$ or $S^4$, let $N\ge2$, and let $P\to M$ be any smooth principal right $SU(N)$-bundle. Fix a smooth reference connection $A_0$, a basepoint $m\in M$, and a frame of $P_m$. Equip the affine space $\mathcal A_\infty=A_0+\Omega^1(M;\operatorname{ad}P)$ with its $C^\infty$ section topology, and let $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ be the connections whose based holonomy action on $\mathbb C^N$ has no nonzero proper invariant complex subspace. Then $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is nonempty and path-connected, and for every $A\in\mathcal A_\infty^*$ and every integer $j\ge1$, $\pi_j(\mathcal A_\infty^*,A)=0$. Here $\pi_j(X,x)$ is the based homotopy group of continuous maps $u:(I^j,\partial I^j)\to(X,x)$ modulo homotopies that keep $\partial I^j$ at $x$.

references.title: I. M. Singer, Some Remarks on the Gribov Ambiguity, Communications in Mathematical Physics 60 (1978), 7–12
references.locator: Theorem 2, p. 9: weak homotopy type; Singer's infinite-codimension discussion is not used as a complete proof.

references.locator: §1, pp. 2–3: Sobolev gauge actions and irreducible connections; no weak-contractibility proof is claimed from these notes.

items.title: Affine filling and the exact reducible-locus repair step
items.design_state: Step 1 argument and contract are complete; current direct and transitive inputs have ready records. This does not claim independent proof approval.
items.statement: Assume ZF together with the Axiom of Choice. Let $M=S^3$ or $S^4$, let $N\ge2$, take the trivial principal right $SU(N)$-bundle $P=M\times SU(N)$, and use its zero connection as affine origin. For any integer $j\ge1$ and any continuous sphere family $f:S^j\to\mathcal A_\infty^*$ of smooth connections on $P$, the cone formula $F([r,x])=r f(x)$ extends $f$ continuously over $D^{j+1}$ in the full affine connection space. The apex is the zero connection, whose holonomy group is the identity and which preserves every complex line, so this affine filling is reducible and does not lie entirely in $\mathcal A_\infty^*$. Relative avoidance changes the filling while fixing its boundary and produces a filling in $\mathcal A_\infty^*$; contraction of the disk to any chosen boundary point gives a based nullhomotopy. The weak-contractibility theorem ensures that such families exist for the trivial bundle and that their based homotopy classes vanish.

references.title: I. M. Singer, Some Remarks on the Gribov Ambiguity, Communications in Mathematical Physics 60 (1978), 7–12
references.locator: Theorem 2, p. 9: weak homotopy type; the affine cone and relative repair are verified locally.

references.locator: §1, pp. 2–3: gauge action and irreducible connections; the example's cone construction is verified locally.

references.title: Dominic Walpuski, Differential Geometry III: Gauge Theory (full lecture notes)
references.locator: §5.13.3, PDF pp. 115–116, holonomy-stabilizer and irreducibility conventions; the cone and relative repair are verified locally.
